scope: Defensive catalog of worm-like and lateral propagation behaviour on Windows. Every entry describes what to record and how to harden; none is a payload, exploit or copy-paste attack command.

techniques.name: SMB admin share copy
techniques.abuse: Uses SMB admin shares (ADMIN$, C$, IPC$) to copy a file to a remote host and then start it through a service, task or WMI. A worm repeats this across every reachable peer.
techniques.probe: Inventory only. The IDS fan-out and lateral heuristics watch the network side.
telemetry: 4688 process creation for net.exe, xcopy.exe, robocopy.exe
techniques.detection: net use or net view against many hosts in a short window. Copy tools writing to \\host\ADMIN$ or \\host\C$. One workstation account authenticating to many peers on 445. Correlate 5140/5145 with 4688.
hardening: Disable SMBv1 and require SMB signing and encryption.
Remove workstation accounts from local Administrators on peers; admin shares need admin rights.
Segment client networks so workstations cannot reach each other on 445/139.
Enable firewall rules that block inbound 445 from client subnets.

tree.p: user or service starts a loader

tree.a: Mounts an admin share for file copy
Starts the copied file as a service

cmd.w: Admin-share paths and net view are the copy-and-spread pattern; normal user file sharing does not target ADMIN$.

asr.n: Block process creations originating from PSExec and WMI commands

net.w: A workstation that opens 445 or 139 to many peers in one minute is the network signature of SMB spread.

fix: Block inbound SMB from client subnets at the host firewall and at the switch ACL.
Remove local admin rights from day-to-day accounts.
Alert on 5140/5145 share access to ADMIN$ or C$ from a workstation account.
Keep the IDS FANOUT and LATERAL_FANOUT rules armed; they name the process and the peer list.

techniques.name: Remote service creation
techniques.abuse: Creates or reconfigures a service on a remote host so the service binary runs with SYSTEM rights. Repeated across peers, this is a common worm lateral step.
techniques.probe: Inventory only. Service creation is visible in the System log and in process telemetry.
telemetry: 4688 process creation for sc.exe and services.exe
techniques.detection: sc.exe with a remote host prefix, create or config, and a binPath outside Program Files. 7045 events with a binary in a user-writable path. A burst of 7045 on many hosts from one account.
hardening: Restrict service creation to administrators and to managed endpoints.
Enable the System log and forward 7045 to a central collector.
Block inbound 135/445/139 from client subnets.
Use AppLocker or WDAC to stop unsigned binaries running as services.

tree.a: Registers a service on a peer

cmd.w: A remote sc.exe create or config with a non-standard binPath is the service-based spread pattern.

asr.n: Block process creations originating from PSExec and WMI commands

net.w: Service control rides 135 (RPC) and 445 (SMB). Watch one host contacting many peers on those ports.

fix: Forward System 7045/7040 to the SIEM and alert on bursts.
Remove local admin rights from standard users.
Restrict inbound 135/445 from client VLANs.
Require signed service binaries with WDAC.

techniques.name: Remote scheduled task
techniques.abuse: Creates a task on a remote host with /s so the task runs a copied binary under a privileged account. A worm uses it to survive and to move to the next peer.
techniques.probe: Inventory only. Task creation is visible in 4698 and in the TaskScheduler operational log.
techniques.detection: schtasks.exe with /create and /s, or /change and /s. 4698 with a task action outside Program Files. Task names that look random or copy a system binary name.
hardening: Enable 4698 auditing and forward it.
Restrict remote task creation with the Task Scheduler security descriptor.
Block inbound 135/445 from client subnets.
Use WDAC to stop unsigned binaries running from task actions.

tree.a: Creates a task on a peer

cmd.w: Remote task creation with /s plus a temp-dir action is the spread pattern.

net.w: Remote task creation uses RPC over 135 and SMB over 445. Fan-out to many peers is the worm signal.

fix: Alert on 4698 from a workstation account to multiple hosts.
Restrict remote task creation to management servers.
Remove local admin rights from day-to-day accounts.
Keep TaskScheduler operational logging enabled.

techniques.name: Remote WMI process creation
techniques.abuse: Uses WMI over DCOM or WinRM to start a process on a remote host. The child process is parented by WmiPrvSE.exe, which hides the original operator from a naive process tree.
techniques.probe: Inventory only. WMI activity is visible in the WMI-Activity operational log and in Sysmon 1/19/20/21.
telemetry: Sysmon 1 process create with parent WmiPrvSE.exe
techniques.detection: WmiPrvSE.exe spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe or a binary from a temp path. WMI-Activity events with a remote client. WinRM 5985/5986 logons from workstations.
hardening: Restrict WMI and WinRM to management hosts with firewall rules.
Enable WMI-Activity operational logging and forward it.
Use the ASR rule that blocks process creation from PSExec and WMI.
Do not give workstation accounts local admin rights on peers.

tree.a: Asks WMI to start a process on a peer
The WMI service starts the payload

cmd.w: Remote WMI execution names a target host and a process-create method; local inventory does not.

asr.n: Block process creations originating from PSExec and WMI commands

net.w: WMI over DCOM uses 135 plus a dynamic RPC range; WinRM uses 5985/5986. Watch one host contacting many peers.

fix: Restrict 135/5985/5986 to management servers.
Enable and forward WMI-Activity operational logs.
Enable the PSExec/WMI child-process ASR rule.
Alert on WmiPrvSE.exe spawning a shell.

techniques.name: Service execution (PsExec pattern)
techniques.abuse: Copies a service binary to a remote host, installs it as a service, starts it, and lets it spawn a shell. The service binary often has a random or tool-specific name.
techniques.probe: Inventory only. The host file is usually absent unless a PsExec-style tool has been used.
telemetry: 4688 process creation for the service child
Sysmon 1 process create; Sysmon 11 file create
techniques.detection: 7045 with a service binary in ADMIN$, Windows\Temp or a user profile. A service that starts and is deleted within minutes. psexesvc.exe or a random service name on many peers.
hardening: Alert on 7045 for binaries outside Program Files and Windows\System32.
Block inbound 445 from client subnets.
Remove workstation local admin rights.
Use WDAC to block unsigned service binaries.

tree.a: Places the service binary on the peer

cmd.w: A service binary in ADMIN$ that is installed, started and deleted in one session is the PsExec pattern.

asr.n: Block process creations originating from PSExec and WMI commands

net.w: The copy and service control happen over 445 and 135. Fan-out to many peers is the worm signal.

fix: Enable and forward System 7045.
Alert on service binaries outside trusted paths.
Block client-to-client SMB.
Enable the PSExec/WMI child-process ASR rule.

techniques.name: Remote Desktop spread
techniques.abuse: Uses saved credentials or a harvested password to open RDP to many peers. A worm can use RDP for manual or automated spread, and ransomware operators use it for lateral movement.
techniques.probe: Inventory only. RDP use is visible in 4624 type 10 and in the TerminalServices logs.
techniques.detection: One account with 4624 type 10 to many hosts in a short window. mstsc.exe launched repeatedly with different /v: targets. RDP from a workstation to another workstation.
hardening: Require NLA and MFA for RDP.
Restrict RDP to jump hosts with firewall rules.
Disable RDP on endpoints that do not need it.
Alert on workstation-to-workstation RDP.

cmd.w: Repeated mstsc targets or saved-credential creation from a non-admin context is the spread pattern.

net.w: RDP is 3389. Workstation-to-workstation 3389 is abnormal in most estates.

fix: Require NLA and MFA for RDP.
Restrict 3389 to jump hosts.
Alert on 4624 type 10 from workstation to workstation.
Disable RDP where it is not required.
